description: The pinned FHIR release, profile set, code systems, unit systems and element scope for the FHIR-to-SULO pilot. Everything SourceContext and MapContract need about the source side. Machine-readable; see profiles/README.md for prose.

release.note: R5 is a separate compatibility track (plan section 1). Element names such as effective[x] and occurrence[x] differ by release, so the renderer refuses any resource whose declared release is not 4.0.1.

source_server.note: Synthetic base used to form canonical resource IRIs and fhir:link targets. No such server is contacted; the pilot never performs network I/O at ingestion time.

renderer.canonical_form: N-Triples, UTF-8, LF line endings, lines sorted bytewise ascending, blank node labels assigned b0..bN by a depth-first walk in FHIR element order

option_notes.emit_code_system_class_assertions: The HL7 publisher adds 'a loinc:33914-3' / 'a sct:702668005' type arcs beside a Coding. That is a terminology-derived OWL class assertion, and concept note section 2 states that a FHIR code literal alone is not an OWL class assertion. Default off. Turned on only by the oracle-conformance test that reproduces HL7's own published Turtle byte-equivalently.
option_notes.emit_ontology_header: The '<...ttl> a owl:Ontology; owl:versionIRI <http://build.fhir.org/...>' block is an artifact of the HL7 publisher and points at build.fhir.org. Default off; on for the oracle test.
option_notes.emit_reference_stub_types: '<https://fhir.example/Patient/p123> a fhir:Patient .' Matches HL7 rendering and gives the source ShEx shape a typed node to match. This is a record-layer type, not a person claim.

notes: entered-in-error is source-only, never rejected: concept note section 2 says it suppresses clinical assertions but does not erase the source record.

Encounter in-progress is source-only pending an explicit policy (concept note section 6: 'may receive a separate, explicitly defined policy; it is not treated as a finished interval'). See reviewer question Q-A2-2.

Agent 3's egfr-source.v1.shex guards Observation.status. R3's answer requires it to widen from ['final'] to ['final','amended','corrected'] so the two layers - ingestion eligibility and map acceptance - agree again. Measured 2026-10-01 with the guard widened locally: egfr-corrected and egfr-amended both map (22 triples each) and egfr-preliminary still correctly fails source validation, so the widening does not leak the verification axis.

R3, answered 2026-10-01: amended and corrected are ELIGIBLE. FHIR's status conflates two axes -- verification (registered < preliminary < final) and revision (final -> amended/corrected). The revision axis does not reduce reliability: both are post-final and have been revisited. Holding them at source-only applied the verification axis's caution to a position on the revision axis, and meant a correction never reached the semantic layer. preliminary and registered remain source-only -- those ARE verification states. entered-in-error remains source-only: retraction, not revision.

Known consequence of accepting amended. MEASURED 2026-10-01, and the measurement does not match the expectation this note previously recorded. An amendment touching only a source_only element (fixture egfr-amended, egfr-456 v3, adds an Observation.note) produces a graph whose triples are NOT identical to its predecessor's under the quality identity mode R2 actually chose. Under 'per-observation' 14 triples differ: 4 provenance (prov:wasDerivedFrom naming _history/2 vs /3, unavoidable) and 10 quality-node triples, because per-observation keys the quality by version, so a purely administrative amendment mints a NEW renal-quality individual for the patient. Under 'persistent-per-person-code' only the 4 provenance triples differ and the expectation holds exactly. Either way the store correctly reports a replacement rather than unchanged, because source_json_digest is a graph-key content field - but the reason differs. R2 was answered provisionally with an explicit instruction not to let the caveat quietly become a conclusion; this is a consequence of per-observation that is worth putting in front of the reviewer. See DR-102 Q-A2-7.

effective_time_coarser_than_seconds.reason: PROPOSED, PENDING REVIEW ITEM R3 - not a settled rule. The reviewer ruled that a date is not an instant; DR-009 derives the consequence that no SULO time node fits a date-precision value. sulo:TimeInstant needs a dateTime; sulo:Duration is an elapsed amount and a date is a position, not an amount; sulo:TimeInterval requires both a StartTime and an EndTime, and deriving those from a date means choosing a timezone the source never gave, which concept note section 2 forbids; bare sulo:Time repeats the bare-sulo:Feature mistake rejected in R4. So the record is retained and no semantic time node is emitted - the same shape as dataAbsentReason.
effective_time_coarser_than_seconds.scope_note: Encounter.period is deliberately NOT in this list. Its open-endedness question is Q-A2-3 / R5 and is owned there, and no Encounter fixture carries a coarse endpoint today. Adding it is a one-line manifest change once R3 and R5 are both answered.
effective_time_coarser_than_seconds.detection: A FHIR dateTime with no time component: the R4 regex makes the timezone offset mandatory once 'T' is present, so 'coarser than seconds' and 'carries no offset' are the same set - YYYY, YYYY-MM and YYYY-MM-DD.

unsupported_modifier_extension.reason: Acceptance matrix row Source fidelity: an unsupported modifier extension blocks semantic materialization. SourceContext enforces this.

temporal_precision_policy.rule: The xsd datatype of a rendered date/dateTime/instant literal is chosen from the lexical form so that precision survives the rendering.

offset_is_mandatory_once_a_time_is_prese.fact: In FHIR R4 the timezone offset is REQUIRED as soon as a dateTime carries a time component. The (Z|(+|-)hh:mm) group sits inside the T-group of the dateTime regex and is not optional, so 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss' with no offset is NOT a conformant R4 dateTime and the renderer refuses it.
offset_is_mandatory_once_a_time_is_prese.source: StructureDefinition/dateTime, the regex extension on dateTime.value, in the published R4 definitions bundle (profiles-types.json). instant requires an offset unconditionally; date never carries one.
offset_is_mandatory_once_a_time_is_prese.consequence: Every conformant R4 dateTime that renders as xsd:dateTime carries an offset. A rule of the form 'emit xsd:dateTimeStamp when an offset is present, xsd:dateTime when it is not' therefore has no reachable second branch at second precision. The only offsetless values are YYYY, YYYY-MM and YYYY-MM-DD, which render as gYear, gYearMonth and date and are never xsd:dateTime. See DR-102 Q-A2-6 and review item R5b.

temporal_precision_policy.unknown_endpoint: An absent Period.end is rendered as an absent triple, never as an invented value. The 'open-ended period' fixture asserts this.

R3_confirmations.scope: Confirms every row of R3 that carried a current value awaiting confirmation. The outcomes below are now the reviewer's, not engineering's conservative holding position.
confirmed: Observation entered-in-error -> source-only (never rejected; section 2: suppresses clinical assertions, does not erase the source record)
Encounter in-progress, planned, arrived, triaged, onleave, cancelled, entered-in-error, unknown -> source-only
value AND dataAbsentReason both present -> rejected (FHIR obs-6)
code not in the pinned set -> rejected
still_open_not_covered_by_this_confirmat: Observation amended / corrected -- the reviewer asked for an explanation before deciding. Held at source-only MEANWHILE, which is their current value, but this is not a ratification.
A 'finished' Encounter with an open-ended period -- no current value to confirm; it needs a ruling and no fixture fabricates it.
The comparator qualified-value pattern (ex:UpperBoundedResult) -- a new proposal, not a row awaiting confirmation. Comparator stays rejected.
N4 Observation.method, and the method-in-the-code rule -- same.
